title: Pilot-scale clover-grass membrane protein concentration and hydrolysate quality observations
citation: Badfar, N., Lübeck, M., Jacobsen, C., & Gregersen Echers, S. (2027). Pilot-scale biorefining of clover grasses for production of food protein ingredients: Interfacial properties, molecular composition, and effects on the physical and oxidative stability of fish oil-in-water emulsions. Food Hydrocolloids, 182, 113048. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.foodhyd.2026.113048. Online full-text record retrieved 2026-11-07.
source_locations: Methods 2.1 (feedstock and membrane processing); Methods 2.2 and Table S1 (crude protein analysis); Methods 2.8 (green-juice feed); Results 3.1 and 3.5 (concentrate composition and proteomics)
license: CC BY, verified on the DTU Research Database record for the final published version. The earlier bioRxiv preprint has a separate CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license and is not the basis for this extract.
material_scope: A commercial blend of 16% red clover, 10% white clover and 74% perennial grasses was harvested on 2023-08-17. The study tested a two-stage membrane process and trypsin hydrolysis of the protein concentrate; it is not a roadside-grass or isoelectric-precipitation study.
experimental_conditions: The article reports approximately 600 kg clover grass processed and 1,330 L total feed volume for first-stage filtration; retentate from a second filtration underwent approximately eight diavolumes. Green-juice feed DM and CP were reported as 3.25% and 16.6%; CP denominator is not specified in the accessible main text. DC was hydrolyzed with 1% w/w Formea Prime trypsin (140 KMTU/g), initiated at 37 C and pH 8 under free-fall pH for 2.75 h, heated to 90 C for 15 min, then centrifuged at 2,000 x g, 22 C, 10 min. CP was measured by Dumas and converted using N x 6.25; n=3 is reported for the CP analysis.
data_scope: 21 reference observations: feed blend shares and pilot scale; green-juice feed volume, DM and CP; diafiltration factor; DC/DCH crude-protein concentrations; selected proteomic quality descriptors; trypsin product activity and dose; and reported hydrolysis/inactivation/centrifugation conditions.
limitations: The feedstock is cultivated Danish clover-grass blend, not Dutch roadside grass or VARTA biomass.
This membrane purification route is a comparator and does not validate GreenHub's current precipitation, centrifugation or product route.

The accessible main text does not identify the mass basis for the blend proportions or CP percentages, and does not reproduce standard deviations from Table S1. The sample denominator for the 1% w/w enzyme dose is not explicit in the extracted method wording.
The reported 600 kg input and 1,330 L stage feed are not paired with complete stream mass, water, solids, protein, permeate or product balances.
No total protein recovery, membrane area, flux, operating pressure, energy, cleaning demand, product moisture or dryer energy is reported in the extracted observations.
The hydrolysate is a separate trypsin treatment of DC; the reported CP percentage is not a protein recovery yield.
No runtime parameter mapping, default, route change, or product-price assumption is derived from this extract.
conversion_or_processing: Values are transcribed from the final article and its reported Methods/Results. No unit conversion, scaling, inferred mass balance, or transfer factor was applied.
uncertainty: Only the CP-analysis replicate count (n=3) is reported in accessible main text; numeric SDs and most process variances are unavailable in this extract.
